_why: AUG-137: the reviewed disposition of every proof in the PRD's 'Success criteria — replayable proofs' section. scripts/replay_prd_proofs.py parses the bullets from docs/prd/xml-spec-graph.md and matches them here by sha256 of the normalized bullet text, so this file cannot silently drop a proof and a deferral cannot be added without editing (and re-reviewing) this file.
_rule: disposition is `required` (the runner replays it on every gate and the verdict fails if it fails or does not run) or `deferred` (recorded as not-run). A deferred entry MUST name `owner`, the board row that owns the missing capability, and `reason`. To re-derive the shas: python3 scripts/replay_prd_proofs.py --print-prd-proofs

proofs.claim: select a board task and get its linked requirement/AC by ID, with exact source anchors and payload bytes
proofs.reason: auger.py carries no board surface (grep -c boardctl auger.py -> 0): resolving a BOARD TASK to its requirement/AC needs the boardctl plan export, which is AUG-119's surface. This runner cannot reach a board task, so the proof cannot be replayed end to end.

proofs.claim: one XML source edit updates every generated spec view, with no hand-maintained duplicate of the source text
a staged change with a missing `ch:trace row=` is named by the checker; GitReins blocks only when configured `block`
proofs.reason: the checker half is reachable (`auger spec check --diff-file` reports `trace-missing-row` at file:line and exits 1), but the proof's second clause — GitReins blocks only when configured `block` — has no reachable surface: no repository enables the spec_alignment guard, which is exactly what AUG-153 owns. Replaying only the first clause would mark the proof pass on half its claim.

proofs.claim: an approved plan writes exactly one canonical boardctl row whose read-back keeps the criteria and spec links
proofs.reason: writing and reading back a canonical boardctl row is boardctl's surface, not auger's; the approved-plan export behind it is AUG-119. This runner has no board writer by design (it never mutates the board).

proofs.claim: one query returns the migration, prior-schema fixture, apply test and assertions; replacing the migration with a no-op makes the named test fail
a false worker claim cannot produce an integration-level PASS from the canonical row plus the XML test obligation
proofs.reason: what counts as judge evidence — excluding the worker summary, refusing a PASS when the named test is absent or red — is the GitReins judge packet, which AUG-124 builds. auger.py has no judge surface, so there is nothing here to replay.

proofs.claim: measured corpus size, selected-bundle size and lookup latency from a reproducible fixture, with the bundle excluding unrelated blocks
the disabled GitReins flag changes nothing and the enabled path leaves no unbounded or orphan process
proofs.reason: the flag and the process-liveness assertion live in the GitReins hook, which no repository enables today (AUG-153). auger.py carries no GitReins flag and spawns no long-lived process on this path, so neither direction of the claim can be exercised from this tree.
